title: Add pseudonymous token-cost summarizer and privacy-hash bridge
author: Priya Mehta
body: Context/Motivation: We need per-invocation token cost visibility without retaining plaintext prompt or response tokens in observability backends. This PR introduces a privacy-first pipeline: (1) deterministic, salted token-hash bucketing at the edge; (2) a compact per-invocation cost summarizer that attributes per-bucket token counts and tokenized-costs; (3) a bridge service that joins hashed token buckets with model cost profiles for rollups and dashboards. Goals: provide accurate cost attribution for SLOs and billing heuristics while ensuring PII/PHI is never logged or exported. Changes are designed to be reversible (config toggles) and auditable. Main changes: - collector: add pseudonymization middleware that applies a per-tenant salt and BLAKE3-based chunked hashing to token fragments, exposing only bucket_id and hash_prefix_size metadata (no token text). - summarizer: a streaming aggregator that emits per-invocation compact summaries: total_tokens, generation_tokens, prompt_token_buckets (list of bucket_id:count), and model_cost_approx_usd (aggregated using model profile). - bridge service: lightweight joiner that maps bucket-level aggregates to model cost model to compute per-route and per-tenant cost metrics used by dashboards/alerts. - dashboards: add a new Observability Pack dashboard panel group 'Pseudonymous Cost Explorer' with per-route aggregated cost and a new 'quiet-surge' alert rule that triggers only when cost growth is sustained across at least 3 hours and >75th percentile of bucket skew. - telemetry: add metrics and labels for pseudonymization_version, salt_id, and summarizer_latency_ms; tracing spans annotated with sample_rate and anonymized_bucket_count. Backwards compatibility: collector can run in dual-mode emitting both legacy plaintext token telemetry (for fast migration) and pseudonymized summaries behind a feature flag. Checklist: [x] design review (ENG-4321), [x] privacy review with security, [x] unit tests for hashing and summarizer, [x] integration test with bridge, [x] dashboard screens, [x] docs draft. Migrations/deploy: - rollout plan: enable pseudonymization off-by-default; stage enable on a small subset of tenants (canary 1%), monitor summarizer latency and cost deltas for 48h, then ramp to 100% over 5 days. - rollback plan: flip feature flag to legacy mode (no schema migration required). - data retention: summarized rows kept 90d; raw hashed metadata kept 7d and then rotated. Security/privacy notes: salts are tenant-scoped and stored in KMS-backed vault; hashing performed in-process so unhashed tokens never leave the collector process. Commit summary: 1) add privacy middleware and deterministic token hashing; 2) streaming summarizer service and proto changes for compact summary; 3) bridge joiner service and query adapters for dashboards; 4) observability pack dashboard panels and alert rule; 5) e2e tests and runbook. Key files changed: observability-pack/pkg/collector/pseudonymizer.go, observability-pack/pkg/summarizer/stream_aggregator.go, observability-pack/services/bridge/joiner.go, observability-pack/dashboards/pseudonymous_cost_explorer.jsonnet, observability-pack/alerts/quiet_surge.yaml, docs/observability/privacy-token-summarizer.md, test/e2e/pseudonymizer_integration_test.go, scripts/bench/summarizer_bench.go, go.mod, go.sum. Tests: added unit tests for hash stability and collision resistance, integration test that validates summarizer output vs synthetic tokenized inputs, benchmark for 99th-pctl summarizer latency. Observability/Alerting: - New metric: pseudonymizer.tokens_hashed_total{tenant,salt_id} - New histogram: summarizer.latency_ms - New alert: observability.quiet_surge_high_cost (suppresses noisy short spikes; logic included in alert yaml) Release notes (short): Adds a privacy-preserving token-cost summarizer that allows cost attribution without storing token text; dashboards and alerts submitted with observability pack. Rollout and monitoring instructions included. Rationale and alternatives considered: we evaluated full differential privacy vs deterministic hashing; deterministic salted hashing was chosen for lower operational complexity and deterministic joins. We added salt rotation support as a safety mechanism. Open questions: - how to present per-bucket explanations to end-users without leaking token content? We opted for statistical bucket descriptors (e.g., average token length, token_type_entropy) rather than examples. - future: consider integrating cryptographic PPE techniques for smaller tenants. Observability runbook excerpt: On spike after enabling, check summarizer.latency_ms, look for high anonymized_bucket_count, and if latency > 200ms for 5m trigger rollback. Compliance: privacy review approved; KMS usage logged.
